Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 25-y-o woman with 2-month history of work-triggered anxiety, insomnia, and morning palpitations; clinical impression is adjustment disorder with anxiety/GAD spectrum, rule-out underlying medical contributors.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive anxiety over past ~2 months, beginning after starting a new, highly stressful fashion-retail head-office job.  
• Symptoms timeline:  
  – Daily dread of leaving the house for work.  
  – Insomnia: bedtime 22:00–23:00, sleep latency “hours,” total sleep ≈3–4 h, shallow.  
  – Early-morning awakenings with palpitations (subjectively irregular, 2–10 min, no true chest pain).  
  – Daytime fatigue, low energy, anhedonia, social withdrawal, stopped running/tennis.  
  – Low mood most days but denies suicidal ideation or past panic attacks.  
• Associated/pertinent negatives: no prior episodes, no syncope, no weight loss, no heat intolerance, no GI symptoms. Appetite unchanged (slightly more chocolate).  
• Past medical history: none mentioned.  
• Medications: none reported.  
• Allergies: not discussed.  
• Family history: mother with history of depression.  
• Social / lifestyle: lives with parents; alcohol—binge on Fri/Sat (likely >14 units/week) plus occasional weekday wine; occasional smoker; no recreational drugs.  

Examination:
• Tele-consultation; no vitals or physical exam performed.  
• No observed distress beyond reported anxiety.  

Impression:
• Most likely: Adjustment disorder with anxiety / evolving generalized anxiety disorder – supported by clear temporal link to new job, pervasive worry, autonomic symptoms, functional impairment.  
• Consider comorbid depressive features – low mood, anhedonia, fatigue.  
• Medical rule-outs (low likelihood but to be screened): hyperthyroidism, anaemia, arrhythmia.  

Plan:
• Provide NHS self-referral link for evidence-based talking therapy (CBT).  
• Share online anxiety-management and sleep-hygiene resources for immediate use.  
• Order basic blood panel (FBC, TFTs, U&E, ferritin ± glucose) to exclude metabolic/thyroid/haematologic contributors to palpitations and fatigue.  
• Arrange GP follow-up 1 week after labs to review results and clinical progress.  
• Safety-netting: patient to call earlier if anxiety escalates, function deteriorates, or palpitations worsen; discuss pharmacotherapy (e.g., SSRI) at follow-up if no improvement.  
• Lifestyle advice: limit alcohol, maintain regular exercise when possible, smoking cessation support.  

Quality checks:

● Missing but expected: medication & allergy lists explicitly, vitals, menstrual history, detailed alcohol units, physical exam findings.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none significant noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear history but lacks objective exam and exact alcohol quantification; no interruptions.
